c74object.name: sunny.events
c74object.digest: Schedule bounded MIDI note lists on Max's global ITM transport
c74object.description: Schedule one-shot pitch/attack-or-zero/release-velocity lists at strictly future integer Sunny ticks. A fixed pool of 256 permanent ITM events is tied to Max's unnamed global transport; in Max for Live that transport synchronizes to Live. This object does not start, stop, seek, rename, or set the resolution of the host transport. Delivery is sample accurate only when Overdrive and Scheduler in Audio Interrupt are enabled, the incoming command reaches the high-priority scheduler before its target, and the downstream Max object supports sample-accurate events. Successful dispatch stops every permanent slot in the equal-tick group before fixed-slot reuse. Relative commands sample that same transport and derive an integer target, but the normal strict-future check still rejects a target made stale by command-queue or scheduler latency.

objarg.name: ppq
objarg.digest: Set Sunny pulses per quarter note in the range 1 to 65535

method.name: event
method.digest: Schedule one MIDI note-on or note-off list
method.description: Tick must map injectively into Max's double ITM domain and be strictly later than the global transport position when the queued command is applied. Pitch is 0 to 127 and velocity is 0 to 127; zero velocity represents note-off. Release velocity is 0 to 127 and defaults to 64. Every output list is pitch, attack-or-zero velocity, release velocity. The help patch explicitly translates that state to xnoteout: it selects attack velocity with a nonzero note flag for note-on and release velocity with a zero flag for note-off. Channel 1 is only a formatting example; no MIDI output port is selected.

method.name: event_after
method.digest: Schedule one event relative to the sampled global transport position
method.description: Delay must be nonnegative. Zero chooses the first Sunny tick whose ITM mapping is strictly after the sampled host tick; positive values add that many Sunny ticks after this boundary. This does not reserve host time: application still rejects a target reached or passed in the interval between sampling and scheduler consumption. Pitch and velocity rules and the output shape are identical to event.

method.name: note
method.digest: Atomically schedule a note-on and note-off pair
method.description: Duration must be a positive integral Sunny tick count, attack velocity must be 1 to 127, and release velocity must be 0 to 127 (default 64). The pair is rejected as one operation if validation, command capacity, event capacity, host timing, or target representability fails.

method.name: note_after
method.digest: Atomically schedule a note pair relative to the sampled transport
method.description: The relative target rule and possible stale-target rejection are identical to event_after. Duration, attack velocity, release velocity, and atomic rejection are identical to note.

method.name: clear
method.digest: Cancel every retained one-shot event in command order

method.name: transport_status
method.digest: Emit the sampled global ITM transport facts used by relative scheduling
method.description: The right outlet emits `transport_status current_tick ticks_per_quarter running transport_name`. Running is zero or one and the name may be the empty symbol for Max's unnamed global transport. The tuple reports one non-transactional observation using only public ITM APIs; it neither mutates transport state nor proves Live identity, event delivery, scheduler priority, or sample accuracy.

method.name: status
method.digest: Post and emit phase-separated command, event, callback, and last-error evidence
method.description: Post the current pending-command count, event-capacity reservations, and events actually retained by the scheduler as distinct gauges. Reserved events include both pending-command events and scheduler-retained events. Scheduled, cancelled, and fired counters require the corresponding SDK scheduling or stopping action invocation; they do not prove host acceptance, callback delivery, host delivery, MIDI delivery, or sound. The right outlet also emits the closed tuple `event_status command_observed scheduled_observed fired_observed cancelled_observed callbacks_healthy reserved_events retained_events last_error`; the left outlet remains the event-list outlet.

method.name: clear_error
method.digest: Clear the retained error without clearing counters or events
